subskill: Range of a constant from floor counts in a linear model
prompt: In a building, floor x is 5x meters above street level, where x is an integer; negative values of x are underground floors, and floor 0 is at street level. A new elevator will stop at every floor whose height, in meters, is at least 2k - 13 and less than 20, where k is a constant. The elevator must stop at street level and at no more than 16 floors in all. How much greater is the greatest possible integer value of k than the least possible integer value of k?
explanation: The elevator stops at floor x when 2k - 13 ≤ 5x < 20. From 5x < 20, x < 4, so the top stop is floor 3 (floor 4, at exactly 20 meters, is not included). From 2k - 13 ≤ 5x, x ≥ (2k - 13)/5, and a floor exactly at height 2k - 13 IS a stop. Street level: floor 0 must be a stop, so 2k - 13 ≤ 0, k ≤ 6.5, so k ≤ 6. No more than 16 floors: the stops run from the lowest stop up to floor 3, so the lowest stop can be no lower than floor -12 (floors -12 through 3 are 16 floors). Floor -13, at -65 meters, must NOT be a stop: -65 < 2k - 13, so 2k > -52, k > -26, so k ≥ -25. So k runs from -25 to 6, and 6 - (-25) = 31. Choice 32 treats 'at least 2k - 13' as 'more than 2k - 13', which lets k = -26 work (floor -13 would sit exactly at the excluded height). Choice 5 uses 2k - 13 as a floor number instead of a height, x ≥ 2k - 13, which gives k from 1 to 6. Choice 39 drops the street-level requirement and only asks that the elevator stop somewhere (floor 3 needs 2k - 13 ≤ 15, so k ≤ 14).
solve: const D=(kEx,wv,noZ)=>{const ks=[]; for (let k=-300;k<=300;k++){ let tot=0,z=false,any=false; for (let x=-150;x<=150;x++){ const h=5*x; const lo=wv? 2*k-13<=x : (kEx? 2*k-13<h : 2*k-13<=h); const up=h<20; if(lo&&up){ any=true; tot++; if(x===0) z=true; } } if ((noZ?any:z) && tot<=16) ks.push(k);} return ks[ks.length-1]-ks[0];}; return D(false,false,false);

quantity_asked: the greatest possible integer k minus the least possible integer k for which the elevator stops at street level and at no more than 16 floors

setup.i: k sets the lowest height an elevator serves in a building whose floors are numbered with integers (height 5x); the top is a fixed strict height
setup.ii: the elevator stops at street level and at no more than 16 floors in all
setup.iii: difference between the greatest and least integer values of k

plugback.why: The ask is a difference between two values of k from two different conditions; 31 cannot be checked by substituting it anywhere. Ascending order reaches the key at try 2, but confirming it needs both extreme values of k, which is the whole solution.

32.why: Reading 'at least' as 'more than' removes the floor at exactly height 2k - 13; whether that lets the range of k grow or shrink depends on which end it affects, which the stem does not show.

5.why: Treating the height 2k - 13 as a floor number changes the scale by a factor of 5 on one condition only; the stem gives no hint of the net direction.

39.why: Dropping the street-level requirement removes the condition that sets the top of k's range; a student cannot see from the stem that the replacement condition is looser.
